title: Render the off-track status marker as an X globally
description: Change STATUS_META.negative.shape from 'diamond' to 'x' in src/lib/status.ts (extend the shape union) and add a .status-dot--x rule to src/styles.css so off-track is told from the on-track filled circle by shape alone, for red/green colourblind readers. Refresh status.shape.test.ts and styles.status-dot.test.ts; the other four shapes stay unchanged. Status is the single shared source of truth, so this changes the marker everywhere it renders (legend, Scorecard, LockedView, builder).

acceptanceCriteria.text: statusMeta('negative').shape === 'x' and the StatusMeta shape union includes 'x'; the other four entries (circle, triangle, ring, half-circle) are unchanged

src/styles.css defines a .status-dot--x rule that draws an X from two crossed bars, reproducing attachment-01.html's `.status-dot.x` off-track marker and visibly distinct in shape from the on-track filled circle
The existing status.shape.test.ts and styles.status-dot.test.ts are updated so `npm test` stays green

rationale: STATUS_META is the one source of truth for status shape across every consumer; a builder-local override would fork status semantics and drift. The change is small and self-contained (union + one map entry + one CSS rule + test refresh), so it is isolated first and every later builder slice inherits the correct off-track marker.

title: Add a DELETE snapshot endpoint and deleteSnapshot dev helper
description: Extend the single dev-write plugin (scripts/dev-write-plugin.ts) with a DELETE branch on /__data/snapshots/:id that idempotently unlinks data/snapshots/<id>.json (200/204, no error on a missing file), reusing SNAPSHOT_ID_RE and resolveDataPath — never a second plugin (ADR-003). Add a DEV-gated deleteSnapshot(id) client in src/lib/devWrite.ts. Both the pulling-screen Cancel and the builder Discard consume it. No UI in this ticket.
acceptanceCriteria: dispatchDataWrite('DELETE', '/__data/snapshots/<valid-id>', …) unlinks the snapshot file and returns 200 or 204; a second DELETE of the same id is idempotent (still 200/204, no error)
A DELETE with an id failing SNAPSHOT_ID_RE returns 400 and writes nothing; the containment check via resolveDataPath still applies and no second plugin is introduced
deleteSnapshot(id) in src/lib/devWrite.ts issues the DELETE and is a no-op returning false outside import.meta.env.DEV, so src/build-purity.test.ts stays green
rationale: Cancel (pulling) and Discard (builder) both need to remove the on-disk draft; making the DELETE branch + deleteSnapshot a single shared slice honours ADR-003's 'extend, never add a second' and avoids two tickets diverging on the same endpoint. Idempotent unlink makes Cancel racing an in-flight write, or a double-confirm, safe.

title: Add the Reviews screen and builder screen-state machine
description: Replace MbrBuilderView's direct-editor mount with a small useState screen machine (reviews → pulling → builder) inside the single DEV-only #mbr view — no new hash routes (ADR-001). Build the Reviews landing: the 'Next up' card for the next unstarted month (latest snapshot's leading YYYY-MM + 1 calendar month in UTC via id.slice(0,7), labelled with snapshotIdLabel; fall back to the current month with no snapshots) and the 'Published' list of prior locked snapshots each with a 'View' that sets window.location.hash to #locked/<id>. 'Pull data & start' transitions to the pulling screen. There is no empty builder state. Bucket/KPI counts are derived from config, not hard-coded.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Opening #mbr shows the reviews screen first (a useState machine reviews → pulling → builder); there is no empty builder state

The reviews screen reproduces attachment-01.html's #screen-start: eyebrow 'Monthly Business Review', title 'Reviews', its subtitle, a 'Next up' start-card (new-pill 'Next up', the next-unstarted month as its heading, a start-meta line of bucket and KPI counts, and a 'Pull data & start' success button), and a 'Published' section-label above a review-list of prior locked months, each a review-row with a lock icon, month name, a 'Published' success state-chip, an 'N KPIs · locked <date>' rmeta, and a 'View' icon-btn
The 'Next up' month is the first calendar month (computed in UTC) after the latest snapshot's leading YYYY-MM, labelled via snapshotIdLabel; with zero snapshots it is the current month
Clicking 'View' on a published row sets window.location.hash to #locked/<that snapshot's id>; clicking 'Pull data & start' transitions the machine to the pulling screen

rationale: The three screens are internal state, not hash routes, keeping the flow local and DEV-only (ADR-001); Reviews is the entry point and owns the next-month derivation and the screen machine every later builder slice extends. Reusing #locked/<id> for View keeps one publish renderer and one hash grammar.

title: Add the Pulling data screen with draft creation and Cancel
description: On 'Pull data & start', create the next month's draft via the pure reconcileRoster(config, latestSnapshot) carry-forward merge and persist it with saveSnapshot, then show the Pulling screen as a presentation of that seeding (no live CLI collection here). Per-bucket rows animate Queued → Collecting… → 'N values pulled', where N counts the non-empty carried values. Cancel aborts the animation, deletes the just-created draft via deleteSnapshot, and returns to Reviews. 'Continue to builder' enables only on completion and enters the builder for that draft. Re-opening with an existing on-disk draft resumes it (builder) without re-pulling.

acceptanceCriteria.text: 'Pull data & start' creates the next month's draft via reconcileRoster(config, latestSnapshot), persists it with saveSnapshot, and shows the pulling screen

The pulling screen reproduces attachment-01.html's #screen-collect: eyebrow, title 'Pulling data · <month>' (month muted after a middot), its subtitle, a top update-progress bar, a collect-list with one collect-row per bucket (accent cdot, bucket name, an 'N KPIs' ccount, and a chip-slot cycling a 'Queued' → 'Collecting…' (spinner) → 'N values pulled' state-chip), and a collect-foot with a 'Cancel' ghost button and a 'Continue to builder' success button disabled until the run finishes
Each bucket's 'N values pulled' equals its count of non-empty carried values; on completion 'Continue to builder' enables and enters the builder for that draft

'Cancel' aborts the pull, deletes the just-created draft via deleteSnapshot, and returns to the reviews screen; re-opening #mbr with an existing on-disk draft resumes it in the builder without re-pulling

rationale: The pull is carry-forward seeding, not live collection — the only reading that reconciles the entry code (reconcileRoster/resume, never a /__collect loop) with the PRD's 'Carried' pill (values open still equal to the last MBR and drop the pill only when the user collects/edits in the builder). Cancel deleting the just-created draft keeps a half-pulled month from lingering (ADR-001).

title: Build the builder core: chrome, status, insight, autosave, completion
description: Port the mockup's builder chrome and editing core into the #builder screen. Render the head (eyebrow, 'MBR builder · <month>' title, subtitle), a toolbar with a Preview control and NO theme toggle (follow the app global useColorMode), the amber draft banner with a warning dot and the autosave meta 'Last edited N min ago · N of M buckets complete', an 'Insights added — N of M KPIs' progress bar, and the bucket-cards with their four-column kpi-head, per-KPI name+sub-line, an editable status-select whose silhouette marker sits beside it, a basic 'This month' scalar value cell, and the insight textarea. Editing status/insight autosaves the whole draft (saveSnapshot). Completion counts use a trimmed-non-empty-insight predicate. 'Last edited N min ago' derives from the snapshot file's real mtime, supplied by the dev-write plugin as a Last-Modified / X-Data-Mtime header on write responses plus a read-side HEAD/stat. Preview renders the exported LockedMBR against the in-memory draft without persisting. Value delta, Auto/Manual tags, manual editing, collect cycle, carried pill, cohorts and lock all arrive in later tickets.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The builder screen reproduces attachment-01.html's #screen-builder head and chrome: eyebrow 'Monthly Business Review', a title 'MBR builder' with a muted '· <month>' period after a middot, the subtitle 'Assemble this month's review from the live scorecard…', a toolbar with a 'Preview' icon-btn and no theme toggle, an amber draft local-banner carrying a warning dot, the text 'Draft — changes are saved locally as you go.', a right-aligned meta 'Last edited N min ago · N of M buckets complete', and a 'Discard draft' icon-btn

Below the banner an 'Insights added' progress-wrap shows 'N of M KPIs' with a progress-fill, and each bucket-card head shows the bucket name, an 'N KPIs' bucket-count and a right-aligned 'N of M insights', reproducing attachment-01.html; every count uses a trimmed-non-empty-insight predicate

Each kpi-row reproduces attachment-01.html's row: the KPI name with a sub-line (metric description + source), the four-column kpi-head labels 'KPI / This month / Status / Insight', an editable status-select with its status-dot silhouette (off-track = X) beside it, and an insight-input textarea with placeholder 'Add an insight for this KPI…'

Editing a status or an insight persists the whole draft via saveSnapshot(id, …); 'Last edited N min ago' is derived from the snapshot file's real mtime reported by the dev-write plugin, not a client clock
Preview renders the exported LockedMBR against the in-memory draft without calling saveSnapshot; the builder carries no theme toggle and follows the app global useColorMode

rationale: This is the editable heart of the builder — the surface where a human sets status and writes one insight per KPI and the month autosaves — so it owns the chrome, the insight-completion predicate that both the progress bar and (later) the lock gate read, and the mtime-derived 'Last edited'. Server-reported mtime is the only authoritative last-write time in a DEV-only, plugin-mediated app (ADR-002). Value/delta/collect/lock layer onto this skeleton in dedicated slices.

title: Add the Discard draft confirmation dialog and shared modal styling
description: Wire the banner 'Discard draft' button to a confirmation dialog and port the mockup's centered-card-over-dimmed-backdrop modal styling (.overlay/.modal) into src/styles.css. The discard dialog frames the action as clearing the month's saved values and insights; confirming deletes the draft file via deleteSnapshot and returns to the reviews screen. Dismissible via 'Keep editing', Esc, or a backdrop click. The ported .overlay/.modal vocabulary is reused by the later lock/unlock dialogs.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The 'Discard draft' button opens a dialog reproducing attachment-01.html's #modal-discard: a centered .modal card over a dimmed .overlay backdrop, a danger modal-icon, the heading 'Discard this draft?', body text framing it as clearing the month's saved values and insights, and a footer with a 'Keep editing' ghost button and a 'Discard draft' danger button
Confirming 'Discard draft' deletes the draft file via deleteSnapshot and returns to the reviews screen
'Keep editing', pressing Esc, and clicking the backdrop each dismiss the dialog back to the builder without deleting anything

rationale: Discard is the first confirmation dialog and the natural place to port the shared .overlay/.modal styling (centered card, dimmed backdrop, Esc/backdrop/Cancel dismissal) that the lock and unlock dialogs reuse. Deleting the draft file plus clearing state is exactly 'discard the month', with no orphan draft left behind.

title: Show value, target, tags and the live 'vs last MBR' delta for scalar KPIs
description: Fill the 'This month' cell for scalar KPIs to match the mockup: a bold value, the roster 'target <t>', an Auto/Manual tag, and a 'vs last MBR' delta arrow. Add a shared tolerant delta derivation — magnitude from the value string (first numeric token, comparators stripped, unit captured), improvement direction from the KPI target comparator, coloured with the MetricStatus positive/negative/neutral tokens — degrading to a neutral, uncoloured arrow on any parse/unit/direction failure. Anchor the comparison on latestLockedSnapshot's value for that KPI; suppress (neutral '—') when there is no locked snapshot. The delta recomputes live on any value change.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A scalar KPI's value cell reproduces attachment-01.html's value-line: a bold val-scalar value, a muted 'target <t>' val-target from the roster, an 'Auto' or 'Manual' tag, and a delta line reading '<arrow> <n> vs last MBR' with an up/down/flat arrow coloured by the MetricStatus positive/negative tokens (flat/neutral uncoloured)

The delta magnitude is parsed from the value string (first numeric token, comparators stripped, trailing unit captured) and its improvement direction is taken from the KPI target comparator; it renders a neutral uncoloured '—' when the number won't parse, the units differ, the target gives no direction, or there is no latest-locked snapshot
The delta is computed against latestLockedSnapshot's value for that KPI and recomputes live whenever the KPI's value changes

rationale: Direction-from-target, magnitude-from-value keeps the arrow honest without adding numeric/unit metadata to the string data contract, and degrading to neutral on any ambiguity prevents colouring a regression green — worse than no arrow for a colourblind-sensitive product. Anchoring on the latest LOCKED snapshot makes 'vs last MBR' literally the last published review (ADR-003). The manual editor and auto collect cycle both build on this value cell.

title: Edit manual KPI values inline with an automatic as-of stamp
description: For manual (empty aiUpdateInstructions) KPIs, render an inline editable value box with a unit and a 'From default view · edit to override' prefill note tagged 'Manual', seeded from the KPI's latest locked value. There is no per-value 'Lock in value' button and no manual 'As of' field — the per-month lock is the only commit gate (ADR-003). Editing stamps an automatic asOf at edit time, persists the draft, feeds a 'was <old> · as of <date>' line, and recomputes the live delta.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A manual KPI (empty roster aiUpdateInstructions) renders an editable value-input with a unit and a 'From default view · edit to override' prefill-note tagged 'Manual', seeded from its latest locked value — with no per-value 'Lock in value' button and no manual 'As of' field, reproducing attachment-01.html's manual PR-review-latency row

Editing the value stamps an automatic asOf, persists the draft via saveSnapshot, and renders a 'was <old> · as of <date>' val-updated line against the last locked value while the delta recomputes live

rationale: The 'From default view' label is literally true only against the locked-only Default view, so the seed is the latest locked value (ADR-003). Dropping the Update-KPIs 'Lock in value'/'As of' ceremony is the captain's settled model — the month lock is the sole commit gate — so a manual edit is just an inline value change with an auto as-of feeding the 'was … as of …' line.

title: Add the per-KPI auto collect cycle with cancellable CLI collection
description: Give each auto (non-empty aiUpdateInstructions) KPI a collect control cycling Collect → Collecting… → ✓ Updated (then Re-collect), with Try again on failure, reproducing the Update KPIs vocabulary. A success applies the returned {value, asOf}, stamps 'was <old> · as of <date>', and recomputes the delta; a failure shows a failed chip + Try again. Wire one shared AbortController from the collect controls through collectKpi's fetch({ signal }); on abort/navigate the sequential work stops and the dev-write plugin detects the client disconnect and SIGKILLs the detached copilot process group (reusing the timeout kill path). Keep collected values in memory until save.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An auto KPI has a collect control cycling Collect → 'Collecting…' (spinner state-chip) → '✓ Updated' then a 'Re-collect' link-mini, with 'Try again' on failure, reproducing attachment-01.html's collect-line vocabulary

A successful collect applies the returned {value, asOf}, renders a 'was <old> · as of <date>' val-updated line, and recomputes the delta; a failed collect shows a 'Collection failed' failed state-chip and a 'Try again' button
Collect fetches through a shared AbortController signal so aborting/navigating cancels the in-flight collect, and the dev-write plugin SIGKILLs the detached copilot process group on client disconnect

rationale: Real /__collect CLI collection is deferred to the builder (not the pull), so the abort/SIGKILL machinery belongs here where a minutes-long CLI can be in flight when the user discards or navigates — otherwise the builder's long collects would be unkillable. Reusing the existing collectKpi client and the Update KPIs collect vocabulary keeps one refresh affordance users already know.

title: Add the amber 'Update all automatically' box and sweep
description: Add the amber warn-line box housing both the caveat and the bulk action: a line stating 'Update all automatically' only collects the automatable KPIs (N of M — those with non-empty aiUpdateInstructions) and leaves the manual ones unchanged, and the 'Update all automatically' button inside the same box. Clicking sweeps only the automatable KPIs in order, each running its collect cycle, behind an indeterminate progress strip; manual KPIs are untouched.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An amber warn-line box reproduces attachment-01.html's: a warning icon, text stating '"Update all automatically" only collects KPIs with automated instructions — N of M' and that the manual KPIs stay unchanged, and an 'Update all automatically' warn-primary button inside the same box

Clicking it sweeps only the automatable KPIs (non-empty aiUpdateInstructions) in order, each running its collect cycle, while an indeterminate update-progress strip shows for the duration; the manual KPIs are left unchanged

rationale: Housing the bulk action inside its warning box means the button and the rule it obeys (only automatable KPIs, N of M, manual ones untouched) are read together. The sweep reuses the per-KPI collect cycle rather than a parallel bulk path, so N-of-M and cancellation semantics stay consistent.

title: Show the purple 'Carried' pill until a KPI is collected or edited
description: Mark each KPI whose value is still the previous MBR's value, untouched, with the purple 'Carried' pill and clock icon from the mockup. Collecting (auto) or editing (manual) the KPI drops the pill. 'Carried' means the current value equals the latest locked snapshot's value for that KPI.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A KPI whose value still equals its latest-locked value, untouched, shows a purple 'Carried' carried-badge with a clock icon, reproducing attachment-01.html's carried pill beside the KPI name
Collecting (auto) or editing (manual) a KPI removes its 'Carried' pill

rationale: The 'Carried' pill is honest only when carried == last locked value; anchoring it on the latest locked snapshot keeps it true, and dropping it on collect/edit is the single behavior this slice owns end-to-end. It depends on the collect and manual-edit slices because those are the two actions that clear it.

title: Render multi-value cohort KPIs with per-source 'vs last MBR' deltas
description: Render multi-value (SubReading[]) KPIs as a cohort-list like the Default view — every sub-reading, no averaging or collapsing — each with its own 'vs last MBR' sub-delta arrow and a 'change vs last MBR' caption. Match each source row's arrow to its counterpart in the latest locked snapshot by SubReading label; an unmatched label renders no arrow. Manual cohorts are edited via the ManualValueEditor label+value-row pattern committing the whole SubReading[] as one MetricValue; auto cohorts are collected wholesale as one reading.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A multi-value KPI renders every sub-reading as a cohort-list (dt label, dd value) with a per-source sub-delta arrow (up/down/flat) and a 'change vs last MBR' cohort-caption, reproducing attachment-01.html's cohort value cell — with no averaging or collapsing
Each source row's 'vs last MBR' arrow matches its counterpart in the latest locked snapshot by SubReading label; an unmatched label renders no arrow
A manual cohort is edited via the ManualValueEditor label+value-row pattern committing the whole SubReading[] as one MetricValue, while an auto cohort is collected wholesale as one reading
acceptanceCriteria.notDrawn: the drawing shows a cohort value as read-only text with a per-source delta and edits a manual value through one compact inline input; it draws no sub-value editor

rationale: Cohort KPIs give per-source trend rather than one blended number, so every sub-reading is shown (like the Default view's cohort-list) and each carries its own delta. Matching by label is the only stable key SubReading offers. This slice builds on the scalar value cell, manual editor and collect cycle it reuses per-cohort.

title: Add per-month symmetric lock/unlock with insight-gated publish
description: Add the toolbar 'Lock month' button and the lock/unlock confirmation dialogs (reusing t-006's modal styling). The lock dialog drops the 'Locked by' handle field, states that locking publishes and freezes the review, and shows a summary of how many KPIs have an insight and how many will publish; its confirm is disabled until every KPI has a non-empty insight (the trimmed-insight completion count). Confirming flips the snapshot to status:'locked' with an automatic lockedAt and freezes every bucket read-only — value, status label and insight static, with a 'Locked' note and an 'Unlock' button in each bucket head. Each 'Unlock' opens an unlock dialog that returns the whole month to draft (per-month, symmetric). Locking no longer writes lockedBy or amendments (both stay optional in shared/types.ts; older snapshots carrying them still render).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The toolbar 'Lock month' warn-primary button opens a lock dialog reproducing attachment-01.html's #modal-lock: a centered card with a warn modal-icon, heading 'Lock <month>?', body stating locking publishes and freezes the review, and a summary of how many KPIs have an insight / how many will publish, with NO 'Locked by' handle field; its confirm is disabled until every KPI has a non-empty insight

Confirming lock flips the snapshot to status:'locked' with an automatic lockedAt and freezes every bucket read-only — value, status label and insight render static, with a 'Locked' lock-note and an 'Unlock' icon-btn in each bucket head, reproducing attachment-01.html's locked bucket-card

Each bucket's 'Unlock' opens an unlock dialog (attachment-01.html's #modal-unlock: accent icon, Cancel / Unlock buttons) that returns the whole month to draft with every bucket editable again; lock and unlock are per-month and symmetric
Locking writes neither lockedBy nor amendments (both remain optional in shared/types.ts and older snapshots carrying them still render); lockedAt is set automatically

rationale: Per-month symmetric lock, insight-gated, with no lockedBy/amendments is the captain's settled model (PRD open questions 1 & 2), so the per-bucket Unlock is a month-wide affordance and the mockup's handle/audit fields are dropped. The insight-completion count is load-bearing — it drives the progress bar and gates the lock — so a single trimmed-insight predicate backs both (ADR-003). Keeping the fields optional lets older locked snapshots still render.
